title: Conrad Biermann's copybook of letters to Danish envoys abroad, Copenhagen 1675 (Rigsarkivet TKUA S-1418)

documents.shelfmark: Rigsarkivet, TKUA Almindelig del, Conrad Biermanns kopibog 1675 (S-1418), pp. [103]-105, Arkivalieronline images 108-109
documents.route: Copenhagen -> Paris (Biermann for the King to Meyercron)

plaintext.source: No decipherment in the copybook; the key sheet is in the TKUA 'Chiffer' 1670-1709 volume, image 55.

transcription.notes: The hook sign is written alike for set1 T (q), set2 A (g) and the number 9 (R); each instance labelled by stroke and checked by context.

system.summary: Each letter has two graphic signs and one number 1-24; names 25-276; an alphabetical code from 279 with open syllables in blocks and words between them.
system.notes: distinct_symbols counted in document A only. Other letters in the copybook use other keys (Spain, early Paris), not yet matched.

prior_solution.where: unknown After the key was found here (26 Oct 2026), Brice Dudout published readings of the image-55 letters to Høeg (eighteen letters, 2 Jan-5 June 1675) and Meyercrone (nineteen, 16 Feb-21 June; 6,103 groups, 99.4%) on Europe chiffrée, 27 Oct 2026, made independently.

conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue task; no other input.

solution.what: Web search for Biermann 1675 cipher, Danish diplomatic ciphers, TKUA Chiffer; nothing printed or online.
Copybook (255 images) and TKUA 'Chiffer' 1670-1709 (309 images) downloaded from the Rigsarkivet image API.
Key volume surveyed by contact sheets; images 1-52, 11 and 77 ruled out (later keys); image 55 (Pomponne 111 / Terlon 112) matched by its syllable values on the first cipher line.
Letter of 23 March 1675 to Meyercron deciphered with the image-55 key: 262/263 tokens give sense.
Image-55 key tried on the 2 January 1675 letter to Meyercron (image 4) and the letter to George Reetz in Spain (image 108 left): numbers do not fit; other keys.
Whole copybook surveyed page by page (survey_A/B.tsv): ~200 letters 2 Jan-24 June 1675, cipher on ~356 page sides; correspondents grouped by number ranges.
Image-55 key tried on Höegk 2 Jan (image 5): reads 'assez indulgent pour prendre la chose sur le mesme pied'; the key covers the Hague family.

All 309 key-volume images dated and 1670s keys (114-116, 145-147, 265, 294/295, 305-308 and others) tested on 10-20-token runs of the Lilienkron, Moscow, Spain, Sweden, Klingenberg, Lincker and early Paris letters; none reads. Image 94/95 fits 9/22 Klingenberg numbers but leaves 13 on blank slots.
Web searches for printed Meyercron and Just Høeg despatches of 1675: none found.

Eleven Høeg letters (2 Jan-9 Feb, 3,216 cipher tokens) transcribed from the images and deciphered with the image-55 key; the sheet resolves 97.2%, context values (new_values.tsv) bring each letter to 98-100% sense.

Values missing from the sheet inferred from repeated use: letter homophones among low numbers (26 n, 31 s, 33 u), names (279 Suédois, 67 l'Empereur, 582 Prince), syllables in the alphabetical gaps (598 que, 702 xe, 710 zo), and the open-square sign = l.

Brice Dudout's readings published (https://bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/documents.html#hoeg-1675, #meyercrone-1675): the image-55 key (his K55) reads the Høeg and Meyercrone letters of Jan-June 1675; the 2 Jan Meyercrone letter is in another key, as the survey here found. Scope here narrowed to Gioë, Schröder and the letters without a key.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key sheet (TKUA 'Chiffer' 1670-1709, image 55) is filed in a separate key volume and had not been connected with the copybook; it reads document A.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_1675-03-23_meyercron.md, cipher tokens of document A only (the other letters of the copybook are not yet transcribed)

gaps.item: letters under the image-55 key (Høeg, Gioë in England, Schröder, Meyercron from late January)
letters without a surviving key (Lilienkron, Gioë Moscow, Reetz, Lindenow, Klingenberg, Lincker, Meyercron 2 Jan, Høeg 21 June, Lente 21 June)
document A p105.24: one open-square sign
